### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0f011fc8af0d4fb34b9e7fa369858a14c1808aee` — the merge of head `dd283faf40257bc209debc3d3aa66e11345f7405` into base `128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0f011fc8af0d4fb34b9e7fa369858a14c1808aee && git checkout 0f011fc8af0d4fb34b9e7fa369858a14c1808aee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce dd283faf40257bc209debc3d3aa66e11345f7405 && git checkout -B drift-repro 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce && git merge --no-ff dd283faf40257bc209debc3d3aa66e11345f7405

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 128b6571f476d4fae347d8f860b04b95927d2cce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72c8a9c8ef32cfa4f4a13df90a767cc11c30f2d8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/32561-exact-read-adopts-pair-row-binding.md, .changeset/32561-pair-row-exact-read-semantic-entry.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.pair-row-exact-read-no-owner.ts + read as cited code, not reviewed: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts outside the diff (`overlaySlotBinding`, `pairRowBinding`, `settledPairRowBinding`, `ownersHoldingAName`, `packageScopedHoldersOf`, `isBundleAddition`, `disablePackage`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts (the one call of `pairMemberWithheldAt`), the pin "a disabled base never promotes a dependent's bundle addition to a holder of the name" in packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.test.ts.

First-round review, read at 2026-11-13T19:52Z. Inputs: card #32561 and its thirteen comments, the PR title and body as they stand, the diff against the merge base `bf02d33b` (seven files, +260 −9), the check-runs on this head, the knock 6863087504. Claim 6863133279. Ruling 6837007729 (residual 3, option C) is read as the card's comments and the PR body quote it; its own text was not read here.

### ① Derived judgments

- The title, the body and the first changeset agree: `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the BREAKING banner, `adr-0087: registered`. The `yes` is the new public method `SchemaRegistry#overlayRowBinding`; the narrowing is the two exact reads and the lists scoped to a package.
- The second changeset carries the ledger entry alone and reads `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right: the entry adds no key and no export.
- The body has no `Skills-docs:` line. A kind other than `none` owes it, and so does a `(narrowing)` arm (M2).
- The declared FROM and TO is not the whole move. One disable shape the body lists under "Unchanged" moves too, by the reading in M1.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/objectql`, `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`: right for a `narrowed` kind. The diff moves both packages, and `objectql` gains a public method.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs at the read: 64 runs, 34 concluded (none failed), 30 in progress, among them `Build Core`, the eight `Test Core` shards and three type checks. Not waited for: this verdict does not rest on them.
- Order. The merge base is `bf02d33b`; `main` is three commits past it (#33142, #33143, #33144), none on a path of this diff. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict.
- `Fixes #32561` closes a card with one open sub-issue (the bare member read that ignores a declared override), which this PR does not touch, as the body says. The seat's.
- The declared-row shape of card comment 6841146506 is measured by the dev in 6863197549 as `main`'s and not moved here. The seat's to route.
- The epic red-line read is owed before ACCEPT, as the knock says.
- The ablations, the local runs and the dogfood battery are the report's; none was run here.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`. The adoption is one line of `pairRowOnAddress`, placed after the four older arms: a declared row, the App's own pair, two owners (refused), a sole owner outside the address's bases. So it can turn a served row into "not this address's member" and nothing else; it cannot serve what was refused or refuse what was withheld. The binding is read lazily and only for an undeclared row with exactly one served owner that is a base. Both callers pass it, so the exact read and the scoped list ask one question, and a registry without the method keeps the older count. This is the shape the card's ruling asks for.

`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `overlayRowBinding`. The method hands `overlaySlotBinding` the composite holders less the disabled ones. That answers ruling C for the case the CONTROL pins (two holders, one disabled). It also changes when the bundle-addition rule is settled, and there the two counts part (M1).

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.pair-row-exact-read-no-owner.ts`. The printed fields carry no tracker id. The remedy is the one the save door already prescribes (`overrides.package`), and the acceptance criterion can be checked at the three addresses it names.

`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`. Residual 1 is pinned in both install orders, with the CONTROL that X served the row before the addition arrived. Residual 2 pins both Apps' package addresses and both pair addresses. The declared-row CONTROL and the disable CONTROL (both registration orders, re-enable refused naming both) can fail. The NARROWING pins read the list and not the execution list (S1).

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix. The adoption counts a disabled holder's addition as an owner, so the enabled holder loses a row the body lists as kept.** Read, not run. `overlayRowBinding` leaves the disabled holders out before the addition rule is settled: `ownersHoldingAName` judges `isBundleAddition` against a `membersOf` keyed by the served set. `packageScopedHoldersOf`, which the exact read takes its one owner from, settles the addition rule over every holder and leaves the disabled ones out afterwards, and `package-scoped-resolver.test.ts` pins that order. The counts part when the disabled holder is the base of an addition. In the names of the residual-3 CONTROL: X and Y each ship `en-US`, Z (on the App and on Y) ships only `fr-FR`, the pair stores an undeclared `de-DE` row, Y is disabled. The exact read counts `[X]`: Z is an addition to Y and stays one. The adoption counts the served composite holders X and Z; Y is absent from `membersOf`, so Z is an addition to nothing there and stays an owner beside X. Two owners bind the row to no package, and the new line answers `not-member`. `?package=X&member=de-DE` then answers X's own `de-DE` (none) where `main` serves the row, and X's lists leave it out. Z ships no `de-DE`, so this is not the residual-1 narrowing, and with Y enabled the read refuses naming X and Y as before. Owed: a pin of this shape in both registration orders, and the count made to agree with it (the addition rule settled over every holder, the disabled owners left out after). If the seat reads the withholding as right instead, it owes a FROM and TO line and a ruling, since it narrows what ruling C kept. If the pin is green on this head as it stands, this reading is wrong and the finding falls.
- **M2 must-fix, on the PR body.** No `Skills-docs:` line. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` owes one, written from the diff. A body edit; no push. A grep of `skills/**` at this head finds the declared form (`overrides.package`) taught and nothing on the exact read of an undeclared pair row, which the line's reason can say if the dev reads the same.
- **S1 should-fix.** The changeset and the body's table declare X's execution list among the narrowed reads. `expectNoOwnersRow` asserts `listed(X)` and never `forSend(X)`; only the residual-3 CONTROL reads the execution list, on the keep side. One `forSend(X)` line in the helper pins the declared answer.
- **n1 nit, a question; no change asked.** The owner the exact read counts comes from `packageScopedHoldersOf`, which also counts a package that holds the name only through its own stored row in the bare slot. `overlayRowBinding` counts composite holders, so for such an owner it would answer the pair itself and the new line would withhold the row. Not traced to a reachable state here. If the seat knows one, it is a second move to declare; if none exists, nothing is owed.

Two must-fix. M1 needs a push, so the delta is this seat's on the new head; M2 can ride the same round.
